jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
Position:
Chief Development Officer
Location:
Remote

Who are we recruiting for?

Executive Integrity is partnering, on a confidential and retained basis,
with a fast-growing US solar and battery storage platform to appoint a
Chief Development Officer. Our client develops a multi-gigawatt
pipeline of utility-scale solar and battery storage projects and is
playing a key role in the region’s energy transition.
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced development
leader to take ownership of a newly consolidated development
function, one that most companies still split across two or three roles,
shaping both strategy and execution across a genuinely high-growth
platform.

What will you be doing?

As Chief Development Officer, you will take full ownership of the
development function, from site origination through to notice to
proceed, across a multi-gigawatt solar and battery storage pipeline.
Working closely with the CEO, the investment team and the board,
you will act as the driving force behind the company’s growth
strategy.

Key responsibilities include:
-Taking full ownership of site origination, land and GIS, permitting,
and state and local affairs across a multi-gigawatt pipeline.
-Leading project and portfolio management from greenfield through
to notice to proceed, including scheduling, budgeting and risk
tracking.
-Building, restructuring and leading a development organisation of
close to 40 people, with real authority over team design.
-Making advance or kill decisions on projects within return and risk
thresholds agreed with the investment team.
-Representing the business to landowners, local and state officials,
transmission owners and offtake counterparties.
-Presenting pipeline, schedule and budget performance directly to
the CEO, board and capital partners.
-Shaping the company’s expansion into new markets and
technologies, including its growing battery storage strategy.
-Partnering cross-functionally with the investment team on capital
allocation and risk, and with construction on project handoff.
-Establishing governance, stage-gating and best-practice systems
across the development portfolio.

Are you the ideal candidate?

-You will bring a strong track record in utility-scale renewable energy
development, together with the ability to build and lead a multidisciplinary
team and operate credibly in front of sophisticated
investors.
-15+ years in renewable or energy infrastructure project
development, with progressively senior responsibility across land,
project management, permitting and stakeholder management.
-A demonstrated track record delivering multi-gigawatt solar,
battery or hybrid projects to notice to proceed, on time and on
budget.
-Deep, current US development market experience, comfortable
with the regulatory and offtake nuance that varies state by state.
-Ideally, a background within an independent power producer or
similarly structured private capital or infrastructure-fund-backed
platform.
-People leadership experience managing a multi-disciplinary
development team.
-Comfortable operating in a private capital or infrastructure-fundbacked
environment, with board and investor reporting experience.
-A bachelor’s degree in engineering, real estate, environmental
science or a related field; an advanced degree is a plus.
-A genuine long-term commitment. This is a five-to-seven-year build,
not a short-term step.

What’s in it for you?

-This position offers the opportunity to lead the entire development
function of one of the US solar and storage market’s fastest-growing
platforms, at a genuinely pivotal stage of its growth.
-Alongside a competitive salary and benefits package, you can expect:
-A rare, single-leader mandate over a function most companies still
split two or three ways.
-Direct exposure to the board and the capital partners behind the
business, with real influence over its direction.
-Backing from patient, permanent infrastructure capital rather than
a fund working to a fixed exit date.
-A performance-linked annual bonus, 100% company-paid
healthcare for you and your family, and a 401(k) match.
-Long-term incentive plan (LTIP) eligibility tied to the value the
business creates.
-The scope to build a team, a function and a legacy from a genuine
blank sheet of paper.
-The opportunity to directly shape how the business enters new
markets and scales its battery storage strategy.

Who are Executive Integrity?

Executive Integrity is a global executive search and recruitment
consultancy for a more sustainable world with a focus on talent within
the Maritime and Renewable Energy sectors. We give a proportion of
all our profits to Renewable World, a charity that develops affordable
and innovative renewable energy solutions to poverty-stricken
communities.
If you’re interested in learning more about this opportunity, we’d love
to hear from you.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
ALL in Education and ALL in Education Fund exist because the future of Arizona is inseparable from the success of its Latine students. While 46% of Arizona’s PreK–12 students are Latine, only 16–17% of school administrators reflect that same community. ALL in Education closes that gap by building Latine leadership, power, and influence across Arizona’s education system, combining deep community leadership development with the power of direct advocacy and civic engagement through its affiliated 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) organizations.
Through programs including the Parent Educator Academy, LISTO Academy, Adelante Fellowship, and Juntos Leemos, ALL in Education has developed over 1,000 leaders, with alumni now serving on boards, in policy roles, and in public office across the state. Having built this foundation, the organization is now moving from its startup roots into an exciting growth phase, and is seeking its next Executive Director to lead that evolution.
The Opportunity

Based in the Greater Phoenix area, the Executive Director will set the vision for ALL in Education’s next chapter, cultivate the partnerships and funders that will fuel its growth, and secure the organization’s seat at the table in the statewide education conversations that shape outcomes for Arizona’s Latine students. This leader will:
Build, sustain, and lead a high-performing, mission-driven team, and serve as primary liaison to the Board of Directors
Serve as the organization’s primary relationship holder with funders, growing and diversifying ALL in Education’s funding base
Lead strategic planning, including finalizing the organization’s strategic plan and advancing its 501(c)(4) advocacy strategy
Build trust across a broad ecosystem of funders, alumni, board members, staff, families, and community allies
Provide strategic oversight of ALL in Education’s portfolio of leadership development and community programs
Set and drive the organization’s policy agenda, and navigate Arizona’s political landscape on behalf of Latine students and families

What We’re Looking For

7–10+ years of senior leadership experience, including 3–5 years in an executive or C-suite role within a nonprofit, advocacy, education, or public sector organization
A proven track record of building and scaling organizations, including developing internal systems and leading teams through growth and transition
Demonstrated nonprofit fundraising experience, with the ability to step into existing funder relationships and cultivate new ones immediately
Experience developing or leading 501(c)(4) advocacy strategy, including familiarity with related compliance requirements
Political acumen and sophistication to negotiate and influence within complex policy environments; Arizona experience preferred but not required
A shared background and lived connection to the immigrant, first-generation, and/or Latine communities ALL in Education serves is strongly valued
Bilingual in English and Spanish strongly preferred

Candidates who advance in the process will receive the full position description and a detailed FAQ about the role, the organization, and the search.
ALL in Education and ALL in Education Fund are committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace. We encourage applicants of all backgrounds to apply.
We are inclusive of all communities Latinidad's

Job Description

The City of Forest Park is seeking an experienced Director of Planning and Community Development. This position carries significant responsibility; the Director is charged with leading the daily operations of the Planning & Community Department by developing a strategy with the goal of providing high-quality services in an efficient and effective manner.

The Director of Planning and Community Development establishes strategic plans, goals and objectives as it relates to building codes, housing codes, zoning, property maintenance codes and ensures the department's strategic plans support the broad City mission. This position provides direction and support to subordinate managers regarding division work plans and ensures the divisions work together to maximize department performance. This position also serves as a member of the Executive Management team, providing input to the City Manager and Council regarding strategic decisions.

This position oversees plan reviews for commercial/residential construction and the inspection process to ensure code compliance. The Director also interprets City ordinances and recommends updates as needed.

The Community Development Director supervises assigned staff, including hiring, evaluating performance and developing benchmarks and performance measures for the department.

The Director is responsible for the allocation of financial resources as well as developing annual operating and capital expenditure budgets for the department. Exercises sound independent judgment, confidently analyzing complex issues, and making timely, well-reasoned recommendations aligned with the City Manager and Council direction and community priorities.

Collaborative Team Builder:
Understands the value of teamwork, empowers staff, fosters cross-functional collaboration, and builds a cohesive, high-performing organizational culture.

Possession of International Code Council (ICC) Building Official Certification highly preferred or the ability to obtain within twelve (12) months will be required.

The Opportunity

Rex is seeking a Managing Director, Capital Formation to build and lead the firm's intermediary distribution engine across independent broker-dealers, hybrid wealth platforms, and tax-advantaged channels. Rex has built a disciplined multifamily investment platform on conservative underwriting and deep, direct investor relationships. This leader exists to turn that foundation into programmatic capital: durable aqueducts of passive LP equity that flow to Rex offerings deal after deal, rather than capital raised one transaction at a time. This role is anchored by three core mandates. First, build the distribution infrastructure: retain and manage a managing broker-dealer, secure third-party due diligence approvals, and clear home-office product committees so Rex earns a place on approved sponsor shelves and every subsequent offering moves through expedited review. Second, activate the selling network: execute selling agreements with independent broker-dealers and hybrid advisory platforms, architect share class structures that serve both commission-based representatives and fee-based advisors through a single desk, and extend Rex's reach onto alternative investment platforms. Third, own the tax-advantaged product pipeline: partner with acquisitions and legal counsel to structure multifamily assets into Delaware Statutory Trusts for 1031 exchange investors, Reg D income funds, and Qualified Opportunity Zone funds that give advisors a home for client gains from business sales, concentrated stock, and other liquidity events. Across all three mandates, this leader wholesales directly to top-producing representatives and wealth advisors while building a high-performing internal and external wholesaling bench. The ideal candidate brings 10+ years of alternative investment distribution experience, established relationships with home-office due diligence teams and managing broker-dealers, command of Reg BI and fiduciary dynamics, fluency in 1031, DST, and QOZ mechanics, and active FINRA registrations. They combine principal-level credibility with the relentless drive of a builder, an architect of systems who protects investor trust with fiduciary discipline and holds their team to uncompromising standards. Must be missionary to the bone, fully aligned with Rex's mission and relentless in pursuit of it. Fully remote.

About The Role

Rex is hiring a Managing Director, Capital Formation to convert a track record of direct, relationship-driven fundraising into a repeatable, programmatic distribution engine. The mandate is to build the infrastructure, relationships, and product shelf that let intermediary capital flow to Rex offerings continuously, rather than being rebuilt from scratch on every raise.

This role owns outcomes across broker-dealer relations, selling network activation, product structuring, and wholesaling execution, ensuring speed, discipline, and fiduciary rigor at every stage. You will operate as the connective tissue between Rex's acquisitions and legal teams, its managing broker-dealer, and the independent broker-dealer and RIA channels where capital ultimately gets committed, translating Rex's underwriting discipline and track record into offerings that clear home-office diligence and win shelf space.

You will architect the systems, share class structures, and wholesaling cadence that convert a single distribution agreement into durable, compounding capital flow, and you will build and lead the internal and external wholesaling bench that carries that reach to top-producing representatives and advisors nationally. This is a hands-on, principal-level role for an operator who has built distribution from the ground up and wants to own the full arc from due diligence approval to closed commitment. Must be missionary to the bone.

Retain and manage a managing broker-dealer relationship, positioning Rex offerings to clear third-party due diligence approvals and home-office product committees.

Recruit, train, and manage a high-performing internal and external wholesaling bench, scaling distribution reach beyond personal bandwidth.

The MPC provides long-range planning, development services, and policy guidance to support sustainable growth, economic vitality, and an enhanced quality of life. It works closely with local governments, community organizations, and residents to manage land use, transportation, and community development initiatives. The Commission emphasizes collaborative decision-making, data-informed planning, and adherence to applicable regulations and standards. Team members contribute to shaping the built environment and guiding future development in the Savannah metropolitan area.
Role Description
The Director of Development Services and Current Planning is a full-time, on-site leadership role based in Savannah, GA. This position oversees the daily operations of development review and current planning functions, including zoning, land use applications, site plan review, and related regulatory processes. The Director manages a multidisciplinary team, assigns and reviews work, and ensures timely, consistent, and compliant evaluations of development proposals. The role involves working closely with elected officials, boards, developers, community stakeholders, and internal staff to present reports, provide professional recommendations, and support public meetings and hearings. The Director is responsible for implementing policies and procedures, improving service delivery, tracking performance metrics, and coordinating with other departments and agencies to support strategic growth and economic development objectives.

Proven leadership and supervisory experience managing multidisciplinary teams in a planning or development services environment.
Excellent analytical, report-writing, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex information clearly to diverse audiences.
Experience working with planning commissions, boards, and elected officials, and facilitating public meetings and community engagement.
Familiarity with GIS, planning software, and data analysis tools used in land use and development review (or ability to learn quickly).
Bachelor’s degree in Urban Planning, Public Administration, Geography, Architecture, or a related field; advanced degree.
Knowledge of Georgia planning statutes and local government development regulations is highly beneficial.
Ability to collaborate effectively, handle multiple priorities, and maintain professional judgment in a fast-paced regulatory environment.

About Us

The American Clean Power Association (ACP) is the leading voice of today’s multi-tech clean energy industry, representing energy storage, wind, utility-scale solar, clean hydrogen, and transmission companies. ACP is committed to meeting America’s energy and national security goals and building our economy with fast-growing, low-cost, and reliable domestic power. Learn more at cleanpower.org.

The Clean Power Institute (CPI) is ACP’s 501(c)3 affiliate organization. CPI’s mission is to build the public support and workforce to fuel the clean energy future. CPI advances its mission through programming that builds a stable, skilled, and diverse workforce and creates strategic partnerships that promote the benefits of clean energy investments across the country.

Position Summary

The Clean Power Institute (CPI) is seeking an entrepreneurial and highly collaborative Executive Director to lead the organization through its next phase of growth. Reporting to the COO of ACP/President of CPI and working closely with the CPI Board of Directors, the Executive Director will lead CPI’s day-to-day operations and develop the strategies, programs, partnerships and resources needed to expand its national impact.

CPI is building a national approach to clean energy workforce development that connects industry, educators, workforce organizations and communities to create stronger pathways into clean energy careers. The Executive Director will identify opportunities for growth, develop new programs and business cases, strengthen and scale existing initiatives, and build the partnerships and financial resources necessary to execute them. This is a hands-on leadership role, with the Executive Director expected to directly develop and execute key initiatives while leading CPI’s broader strategy and growth.

CPI’s relationship with ACP provides direct access to the companies investing in, building, operating and supplying America’s clean energy infrastructure. The Executive Director will leverage that connection to ensure CPI’s workforce and education programs respond to real industry needs, while expanding CPI’s partnerships across philanthropy, education, workforce development and communities nationwide.

Essential Functions/Major Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Other duties may be assigned to meet business needs.

Strategy & Organizational Growth

Lead the development and execution of CPI’s long-term vision, strategy, and operating priorities in partnership with the CPI Board of Directors and ACP leadership.
Build the organizational capabilities, team, systems, partnerships, and resources necessary to grow CPI from a portfolio of successful initiatives into an integrated national platform.
Identify opportunities for new programs, partnerships, and areas of growth; develop strategies and business cases to evaluate opportunities and bring forward recommendations for investment and execution.
Establish CPI as a nationally recognized leader and convener on clean energy workforce development, education, economic opportunity, and community engagement.
Establish clear goals and measures of success across CPI’s work and ensure accountability for execution and results.

Programs, Workforce & Education

Lead a national workforce strategy focused on building sustainable talent pipelines in the communities where clean energy projects are developed and operated, particularly rural communities.
Build upon CPI’s existing workforce models and expand its reach across wind, solar, energy storage, transmission, electrical trades, manufacturing, and emerging clean energy careers.
Lead the creation of an integrated education-to-career strategy that introduces students to clean energy early and connects them through high school, community colleges, apprenticeships, universities, military pathways, and employment.
Build partnerships with K–12 systems, educators, community colleges, and national youth-serving organizations to dramatically expand clean energy career awareness.
Lead the development and growth of the Clean Energy Academy as the industry’s premier learning platform and the educational backbone of CPI’s national workforce strategy.
Ensure the Academy connects early career awareness, workforce preparation, professional development, and lifelong learning into a cohesive educational ecosystem.
Use data, partner feedback, and program outcomes to evaluate impact, identify opportunities, and guide the continued growth of CPI’s programs.

Partnerships, Fundraising & External Engagement

Serve as CPI’s chief fundraiser and develop a comprehensive, diversified fundraising strategy capable of supporting CPI’s national ambitions.
Build and maintain strong relationships with foundations, corporations, individual philanthropists, and other institutional funders interested in clean energy, workforce development, education, economic mobility, rural communities, STEM, and the future of work.
Develop a compelling philanthropic case for investment that connects CPI’s workforce and education mission with economic opportunity, community impact, and the long-term strength of American clean energy.
Ensure strong stewardship of philanthropic investments through measurable outcomes, effective reporting, compelling storytelling, and sustained relationships with funders.
Build a national network of strategic partnerships across philanthropy, education, workforce development, youth-serving organizations, economic development organizations, and state and regional clean energy associations.
Serve as a national convener capable of bringing organizations with different perspectives and capabilities together around shared workforce and education challenges.
Work with state and regional organizations to translate CPI’s national strategy into locally relevant programs and resources, recognizing that clean energy projects ultimately succeed at the community level.
Serve as CPI’s principal external ambassador and a compelling national voice on clean energy workforce development, education, economic opportunity, and community impact.
Represent CPI with CEOs and industry leaders, philanthropic organizations, policymakers, educators, workforce leaders, community organizations, conferences, media, and other national forums.
Build CPI’s national profile and reputation as a trusted, solutions-oriented organization capable of bringing industry and external partners together to solve complex workforce and education challenges.

Organizational Leadership

Lead CPI’s day-to-day operations and team, establishing clear priorities, accountability, and expectations across the organization.
Develop a strong and highly collaborative partnership with the CPI Board of Directors, engaging the Board as strategic advisors, ambassadors, fundraisers, and champions of CPI’s mission.
Engage individual Board members strategically based on their expertise, relationships, and ability to advance CPI’s priorities, including industry engagement, fundraising, partnerships, and external visibility.
Provide the Board with clear updates on CPI’s performance, major initiatives, and emerging opportunities, and bring forward significant strategic priorities and recommendations for Board consideration.
Make CPI’s relationship with ACP and its member companies a defining strategic advantage for the organization.
Engage ACP member companies not simply as employers at the end of the talent pipeline, but as partners in identifying workforce needs, shaping curricula and credentials, providing career exposure, creating internships and apprenticeships, and investing in workforce solutions.
Position CPI as the place where the clean energy industry can collectively address workforce and talent challenges that individual companies cannot solve alone.
Work collaboratively with ACP leadership and staff, leveraging ACP’s industry expertise, relationships, and organizational resources while establishing a strong identity, strategy, and external presence for CPI.
Lead and develop CPI staff, establishing clear expectations and accountability while building an entrepreneurial and collaborative organizational culture.
Assess CPI’s organizational and staffing needs as the organization grows and recommend the structure, talent, and resources necessary to support its priorities.

15+ years of progressively responsible leadership experience, including significant experience in a senior organizational, program, or executive leadership role. Experience in clean energy, workforce development, education, philanthropy, economic development, nonprofit leadership, government, or a related field is strongly preferred.

Demonstrated ability to develop long-term strategy, translate broad organizational goals into actionable plans, and lead complex programs or initiatives from concept through execution and evaluation.
Hands-on, execution-oriented leadership style with the ability to move between strategy and direct execution as needed to advance CPI’s priorities.
Strong business and financial acumen, including experience developing business cases, managing budgets and resources, evaluating investments and opportunities, and making recommendations that support organizational growth and long-term sustainability.
Proven fundraising and resource development experience, with the ability to build relationships and secure support from corporations, foundations, government entities, philanthropic partners, and other funders.
